name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q01 - Polymer of glucose stored by animals

questiontext.text: 1. Which of the following polymers of glucose is stored by animals?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Polysaccharides are naturally occurring polymers of monosaccharides such as glucose. Different organisms store glucose in structurally distinct polymeric forms depending on their metabolic needs.

Step 2: Evaluation
Cellulose is a structural polysaccharide found in plant cell walls. Amylose and amylopectin are the two components of starch, which serves as the primary reserve carbohydrate in plants. Glycogen is a highly branched polymer of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose (similar in structure to amylopectin but more extensively branched) that is synthesised and stored in the liver and muscles of animals.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The polymer of glucose stored by animals is Glycogen.

questiontext.text: 2. Which of the following is not a semisynthetic polymer?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Based on their source, polymers are classified into natural polymers (obtained directly from plants and animals), semisynthetic polymers (chemically modified natural polymers), and synthetic polymers (man-made).

Step 2: Evaluation
Cellulose nitrate and cellulose acetate (rayon) are obtained by chemical modification of natural cellulose, making them semisynthetic polymers. Vulcanised rubber is prepared by heating natural rubber with sulphur to introduce cross-links, so it is also a semisynthetic polymer. In contrast, cis-polyisoprene is natural rubber itself, obtained directly from rubber latex without chemical modification.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The polymer that is not semisynthetic is cis-polyisoprene.

questiontext.text: 3. The commercial name of polyacrylonitrile is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Polyacrylonitrile (PAN) is an addition polymer formed by the free-radical polymerisation of acrylonitrile (\(\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CN}\)) in the presence of a peroxide catalyst.

Step 2: Evaluation
Polyacrylonitrile is used as a substitute for wool in making commercial fibres and is marketed under the trade names Orlon or Acrilan. Dacron is a polyester (polyethylene terephthalate), PVC is polyvinyl chloride, and Bakelite is a phenol-formaldehyde resin.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The commercial name of polyacrylonitrile is Orlon (acrilan).

questiontext.text: 4. Which of the following polymer is biodegradable?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biodegradable polymers contain functional groups (such as ester or amide linkages) similar to those present in biopolymers, allowing them to be broken down by microorganisms in the environment.

Step 2: Evaluation
Polychloroprene (neoprene) and hydrocarbon addition copolymers such as Buna-S have strong carbon-carbon backbones that resist microbial degradation. Nylon 6,6 is a synthetic polyamide that is also non-biodegradable. In contrast, poly-\(\beta\)-hydroxybutyrate-co-\(\beta\)-hydroxyvalerate (PHBV), formed by the copolymerisation of 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid, contains hydrolysable aliphatic ester linkages and undergoes bacterial degradation in the environment.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The biodegradable polymer among the given structures is PHBV, the aliphatic polyester formed from 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid.

questiontext.text: 5. In which of the following polymers ethylene glycol is one of the monomer units?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ethylene glycol (\(\mathrm{HO}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{OH}\)) is a dihydric alcohol that undergoes condensation polymerisation with dicarboxylic acids to form polyesters containing the \(-\mathrm{OCH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{OOC}-\) repeating unit.

Step 2: Evaluation
Polythene is an addition polymer of ethene. Buna-S is an addition copolymer of 1,3-butadiene and styrene. PHBV is a polyester of 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid. Glyptal is a polyester formed by the condensation of ethylene glycol with phthalic acid (benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid), and its repeating unit clearly contains the \(-\mathrm{OCH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{OOC}-\) linkage attached to an ortho-disubstituted benzene ring.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The polymer having ethylene glycol as one of its monomer units is Glyptal.

questiontext.text: 6. Which of the following statements is not true about low density polythene?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Low density polythene (LDPE) is obtained by the polymerisation of ethene under high pressure (\(1000\) to \(2000\text{ atm}\)) and high temperature (\(350\) to \(570\text{ K}\)) in the presence of traces of dioxygen or a peroxide initiator via a free-radical mechanism.

Step 2: Evaluation
Because of H-atom abstraction during free-radical polymerisation, LDPE has a highly branched structure. These branches prevent close packing of polymer chains, resulting in low density. Consequently, LDPE is chemically inert, tough, flexible (not hard), and a poor conductor of electricity. Hardness is a characteristic property of high density polythene (HDPE), which has linear chains.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement that is not true about low density polythene is that it is Hard.

questiontext.text: 7. \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}-\right)_{n}\) is a polymer having monomer units

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The given polymer repeating unit is \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}-\right)_{n}\), which represents polyisobutylene.

Step 2: Relevant Principle
Addition polymers are formed by breaking the \(\pi\)-bond of an unsaturated alkene monomer and linking the carbons head-to-tail to form the polymer backbone.

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working
Splitting the repeating unit into two-carbon segments gives \(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}-\). Reforming the carbon-carbon double bond between these two carbons yields the monomer \(\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}\) (2-methylpropene or isobutylene).

Step 4: Final Answer
The monomer unit of the given polymer is 2-methylpropene (\(\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}\)).

questiontext.text: 8. Which of the following polymer can be formed by using the following monomer unit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The given cyclic amide structure is caprolactam, a 7-membered ring containing five \(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\) groups and one \(-\mathrm{NH}-\mathrm{C}(=\mathrm{O})-\) amide group (6 carbon atoms in total).

Step 2: Evaluation
Heating caprolactam with water at a high temperature (\(533\)–\(543\text{ K}\)) causes ring-opening polymerisation to form a linear polyamide with six carbon atoms per repeating unit, \(\left[-\mathrm{NH}-(\mathrm{CH}_{2})_{5}-\mathrm{C}(=\mathrm{O})-\right]_{n}\), known as Nylon-6. Nylon 6,6 is formed from hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid; Nylon 2-nylon 6 is formed from glycine and aminocaproic acid; melamine polymer is formed from melamine and formaldehyde.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The polymer formed from caprolactam is Nylon-6.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q09 - Polymers requiring at least one diene monomer

questiontext.text: 9. Which of the following polymers, need at least one diene monomer for their preparation?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A diene monomer contains two carbon-carbon double bonds and is commonly used in the synthesis of synthetic rubbers (elastomers) by addition polymerisation.

Step 2: Evaluation
Buna-S is a copolymer of 1,3-butadiene (a conjugated diene) and styrene. Neoprene is a homopolymer of chloroprene (2-chloro-1,3-butadiene, also a conjugated diene). In contrast, Dacron is a polyester made from ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid, and Novolac is a linear phenol-formaldehyde condensation polymer; neither requires a diene monomer.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The polymers that require at least one diene monomer are Buna-S and Neoprene.

questiontext.text: 10. Which of the following are characteristics of thermosetting polymers?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Thermosetting polymers are cross-linked or heavily branched molecules that undergo extensive cross-linking in moulds upon heating.

Step 2: Evaluation
Because of their three-dimensional network of strong covalent cross-links, thermosetting polymers are heavily branched cross-linked polymers and become permanently infusible on moulding, meaning they cannot be remelted or reused. Linear or slightly branched long-chain molecules that soften on heating and harden on cooling (and can be reused) are characteristics of thermoplastic polymers, not thermosetting polymers.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The characteristics of thermosetting polymers are that they are heavily branched cross linked polymers and become infusible on moulding so cannot be reused.

answer.text: Become infusible on moulding so cannot be reused.
Soften on heating and harden on cooling, can be reused.

questiontext.text: 11. Which of the following polymers are thermoplastic?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Thermoplastic polymers are linear or slightly branched long-chain polymers whose intermolecular forces are intermediate between elastomers and fibres; they soften repeatedly on heating and harden on cooling.

Step 2: Evaluation
Teflon (polytetrafluoroethene) and polystyrene are linear addition polymers that behave as thermoplastics. In contrast, natural rubber (cis-polyisoprene) and neoprene (polychloroprene) have weak van der Waals forces between coiled chains and are classified as elastomers.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The thermoplastic polymers are Teflon and Polystyrene.

questiontext.text: 12. Which of the following polymers are used as fibre?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fibres are thread-forming solids that possess high tensile strength and high modulus due to strong intermolecular forces such as hydrogen bonding or dipole-dipole interactions, leading to close packing of chains.

Step 2: Evaluation
Nylon (a polyamide) and Terylene (a polyester) have strong intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonding in nylons and dipole-dipole interactions in polyesters) and are widely used as synthetic fibres. Polytetrafluoroethene (Teflon) is used as a non-stick thermoplastic coating, and polychloroprene (neoprene) is a synthetic rubber (elastomer).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The polymers used as fibres are Nylon and Terylene.

questiontext.text: 13. Which of the following are addition polymers?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Addition polymers are formed by the repeated addition of monomer molecules possessing double or triple bonds without the elimination of any small molecules.

Step 2: Evaluation
Orlon (polyacrylonitrile, formed from \(\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CN}\)) and polystyrene (formed from \(\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}_{2}\)) are both formed by free-radical addition polymerisation. Nylon and melamine formaldehyde resin are formed by condensation polymerisation with the elimination of small molecules such as water.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The addition polymers are Orlon and Polystyrene.

questiontext.text: 14. Which of the following polymers are condensation polymers?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Condensation polymers are formed by repeated condensation reactions between two different bifunctional or trifunctional monomeric units, accompanied by the elimination of small molecules such as water, alcohol, or \(\mathrm{HCl}\).

Step 2: Evaluation
Bakelite is formed by the condensation of phenol and formaldehyde, and melamine formaldehyde resin is formed by the condensation of melamine and formaldehyde; both eliminate water molecules during polymerisation. Teflon (from tetrafluoroethene) and butyl rubber (from isobutylene and isoprene) are addition polymers.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The condensation polymers are Bakelite and Melamine formaldehyde resin.

questiontext.text: 15. Which of the following monomers form biodegradable polymers?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Synthetic biodegradable polymers are designed with hydrolysable functional groups (such as aliphatic ester or peptide-like amide linkages) that can be cleaved by microorganisms.

Step 2: Evaluation
3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid copolymerise to form PHBV (poly-\(\beta\)-hydroxybutyrate-co-\(\beta\)-hydroxyvalerate), a biodegradable polyester. Glycine and aminocaproic acid copolymerise to form Nylon 2-nylon 6, an alternating polyamide that is also biodegradable. In contrast, ethylene glycol with phthalic acid forms Glyptal and caprolactam forms Nylon-6, both of which are non-biodegradable.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The monomer pairs that form biodegradable polymers are 3-hydroxybutanoic acid + 3-hydroxypentanoic acid and Glycine + amino caproic acid.

questiontext.text: 16. Which of the following are example of synthetic rubber?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Synthetic rubbers are vulcanisable, rubber-like synthetic polymers capable of stretching to at least twice their length and returning to their original shape upon release of the external force.

Step 2: Evaluation
Polychloroprene (neoprene) and Buna-N (copolymer of 1,3-butadiene and acrylonitrile) are well-known synthetic rubbers. Polyacrylonitrile (Orlon) is a synthetic fibre, while cis-polyisoprene is natural rubber obtained from latex.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The examples of synthetic rubber are Polychloroprene and Buna-N.

questiontext.text: 17. Which of the following polymers can have strong intermolecular forces?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Among linear polymers, fibres possess the strongest intermolecular forces (such as hydrogen bonding and dipole-dipole interactions), whereas elastomers have the weakest forces and thermoplastics have intermediate forces.

Step 2: Evaluation
Nylon (a polyamide) exhibits strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding between \(-\mathrm{NH}-\) and \(-\mathrm{C}(=\mathrm{O})-\) groups, and polyesters (such as Terylene) exhibit strong dipole-dipole interactions due to polar ester groups. Rubber is an elastomer with weak van der Waals forces, and polystyrene is a thermoplastic with intermediate van der Waals forces.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The polymers that have strong intermolecular forces are Nylon and Polyesters.

questiontext.text: 18. Which of the following polymers have vinylic monomer units?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vinylic monomers are ethene or substituted ethene molecules containing a \(\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}\) double bond (general form \(\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{X}\) or \(\mathrm{CF}_{2}=\mathrm{CF}_{2}\)) that undergo addition polymerisation.

Step 2: Evaluation
Acrilan (polyacrylonitrile) is formed from acrylonitrile (\(\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CN}\)), polystyrene is formed from styrene (\(\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\)), and Teflon is formed from tetrafluoroethene (\(\mathrm{CF}_{2}=\mathrm{CF}_{2}\)); all three are derived from vinylic monomers. Nylon is a polyamide formed by condensation polymerisation of diamines and dicarboxylic acids (or ring-opening of caprolactam), so it does not have vinylic monomer units.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The polymers having vinylic monomer units are Acrilan, Polystyrene, and Teflon.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q19 - Effect of vulcanisation on natural rubber

questiontext.text: 19. Vulcanisation makes rubber

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vulcanisation is the process of heating raw natural rubber with sulphur (and an appropriate additive) at \(373\text{ K}\) to \(415\text{ K}\), which introduces sulphur cross-links at the reactive allylic sites between polymer chains.

Step 2: Evaluation
These disulphide (\(-\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}-\)) cross-links prevent the polymer chains from slipping past each other permanently when stretched, thereby making the rubber more elastic and more stiff (increasing its tensile strength and hardness). Vulcanised rubber remains amorphous (not crystalline) and becomes insoluble in common solvents.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Vulcanisation makes rubber more elastic and more stiff.

questiontext.text: 38. Match the polymer of Column I with correct monomer of Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Addition polymers are named after or derived from the unsaturated monomer units that undergo chain-growth polymerisation.

Step 2: Evaluation
High density polythene (HDP) is formed by the coordination polymerisation of ethene. Neoprene is a synthetic rubber formed by the free-radical polymerisation of chloroprene (2-chloro-1,3-butadiene). Natural rubber is a linear polymer of isoprene (2-methyl-1,3-butadiene). Teflon (polytetrafluoroethene) is obtained from tetrafluoroethene. Acrilan (polyacrylonitrile) is prepared from acrylonitrile.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
High density polythene matches with Ethene; Neoprene matches with Chloroprene; Natural rubber matches with Isoprene; Teflon matches with Tetrafluoroethene; Acrilan matches with Acrylonitrile.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_POLYMERS_MATCH_Q39 - Matching polymers with their chemical names

questiontext.text: 39. Match the polymers given in Column I with their chemical names given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Commercial or common polymer names correspond to systematic chemical names based on their repeating monomer units.

Step 2: Evaluation
Nylon 6 is obtained by ring-opening polymerisation of caprolactam, so its chemical name is polycaprolactam. PVC stands for polyvinyl chloride. Acrilan is the commercial name for polyacrylonitrile. Natural rubber is chemically cis-1,4-polyisoprene. LDP stands for low density polythene.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Nylon 6 matches with Polycaprolactum; PVC matches with Polyvinyl chloride; Acrilan matches with Polyacrylonitrile; Natural rubber matches with cis-polyisoprene; LDP matches with Low density polythene.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_POLYMERS_MATCH_Q40 - Matching polymers with their commercial names

questiontext.text: 40. Match the polymers given in Column I with their commercial names given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Copolymers and condensation polymers are commonly known by their industrial or commercial trade names.

Step 2: Evaluation
The polyester of ethylene glycol and phthalic acid is Glyptal. The copolymer of 1,3-butadiene and styrene is Buna-S. The linear condensation resin of phenol and formaldehyde is Novolac. The polyester of ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid is Dacron (Terylene). The copolymer of 1,3-butadiene and acrylonitrile is Buna-N.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Polyester of glycol and phthalic acid matches with Glyptal; Copolymer of 1, 3-butadiene and styrene matches with Buna-S; Phenol and formaldehyde resin matches with Novolac; Polyester of glycol and terephthalic acid matches with Dacron; Copolymer of 1, 3-butadiene and acrylonitrile matches with Buna-N.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_POLYMERS_MATCH_Q41 - Matching polymers with their main applications

questiontext.text: 41. Match the polymers given in Column I with their main applications given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The practical application of a polymer depends on its mechanical strength, thermal stability, chemical inertness, and electrical insulating properties.

Step 2: Evaluation
Bakelite is a thermosetting electrical insulator used for making electrical switches. Low density polythene is chemically inert, tough, and flexible, making it suitable for squeeze bottles. Melamine-formaldehyde resin is hard and unbreakable, used in unbreakable crockery. Nylon 6 has high tensile strength and is used for tyre cords. Polytetrafluoroethane (Teflon) is chemically inert and heat resistant, used in non-stick cookwares. Polystyrene (in expanded/foam form) is used as packaging material for shock absorbance.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Bakelite matches with Electrical switches; Low density polythene matches with Squeeze bottles; Melamine-formaldehyde resin matches with Unbreakable crockery; Nylon 6 matches with Tyre, cords; Polytetrafluoroethane matches with Non-stick cookwares; Polystyrene matches with Packaging material for shock absorbance.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_POLYMERS_MATCH_Q42 - Matching polymers with preferred mode of polymerisation

questiontext.text: 42. Match the polymers given in Column I with the preferred mode of polymerisation followed by their monomers.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Different monomers polymerise via distinct mechanisms: bifunctional monomers undergo condensation polymerisation, vinylic monomers commonly undergo free-radical polymerisation, and ethene forms linear high density polythene using coordination catalysts.

Step 2: Evaluation
Nylon-6,6 is formed by the step-growth condensation polymerisation of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid with the elimination of water. PVC is produced by the free-radical addition polymerisation of vinyl chloride. High density polythene (HDP) is synthesised by Ziegler-Natta (coordination) polymerisation of ethene in the presence of triethylaluminium and titanium tetrachloride.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Nylon-6,6 matches with Condensation polymerisation; PVC matches with Free radical polymerisation; HDP matches with Ziegler-Natta polymerisation or coordination polymerisation.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_POLYMERS_MATCH_Q43 - Matching polymers with type of linkage

questiontext.text: 43. Match the polymers given in Column I with the type of linkage present in them given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Condensation polymers and biopolymers are characterised by the specific covalent linkage formed between their monomeric units.

Step 2: Evaluation
Terylene is a polyester containing ester linkages (\(-\mathrm{COO}-\)). Nylon is a synthetic polyamide containing amide linkages (\(-\mathrm{CONH}-\)). Cellulose is a polysaccharide composed of \(\beta\)-D-glucose units joined by glycosidic linkages. Proteins are natural polyamides of \(\alpha\)-amino acids joined by peptide (amide) linkages. RNA is a polynucleotide in which nucleotides are joined by phosphodiester linkages.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Terylene matches with Ester linkage; Nylon matches with Amide linkage; Cellulose matches with Glycosidic linkage; Protein matches with Amide linkage; RNA matches with Phosphodiester linkage.

questiontext.text: 44. Match materials given in Column I with the polymers given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Specific everyday and industrial materials are manufactured from characteristic polymers with matching physical and chemical properties.

Step 2: Evaluation
Natural rubber latex is a colloidal dispersion of cis-polyisoprene. Wood laminates and laminated sheets are made using urea-formaldehyde resins. Ropes and fibres are made from Nylon due to its high tensile strength. Polyester fabric is made from Dacron (Terylene). Neoprene is a widely used synthetic rubber. Unbreakable crockery is manufactured from melamine-formaldehyde resins.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Natural rubber latex matches with cis-polyisoprene; Wood laminates matches with Urea-formaldehyde resins; Ropes and fibres matches with Nylon; Polyester fabric matches with Dacron; Synthetic rubber matches with Neoprene; Unbreakable crockery matches with Melamine formaldehyde resins.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_POLYMERS_MATCH_Q45 - Matching polymers with their repeating units

questiontext.text:
45. Match the polymers given in Column I with their repeating units given in Column II.

Column II:

(a) \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{Cl})-\right)_{n}\)

(b) \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{Cl})=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\right)_{n}\)

(c) \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CN})-\right)_{n}\)

(d) \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CN})-\right)_{n}\)

(f) \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5})-\right)_{n}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each polymer is uniquely identified by the chemical structure of its repeating monomeric unit.

Step 2: Evaluation
Acrilan (polyacrylonitrile) has the repeating unit \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CN})-\right)_{n}\). Polystyrene has the phenyl-substituted repeating unit \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5})-\right)_{n}\). Neoprene (polychloroprene) has the repeating unit \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{Cl})=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\right)_{n}\). Novolac is a linear phenol-formaldehyde polymer consisting of phenolic rings linked by \(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\) bridges. Buna-N is a copolymer of 1,3-butadiene and acrylonitrile, giving \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CN})-\right)_{n}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Acrilan matches with (d); Polystyrene matches with (f); Neoprene matches with (b); Novolac matches with (e); Buna-N matches with (c).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_AR_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q46 - Rayon as a semisynthetic polymer and acetylation of cellulose

questiontext.text:
46. Assertion : Rayon is a semi synthetic polymer and is taken as a better choice than cotton fabric.

Reason : Mechanical and aesthetic properties of cellulose can be improved by acetylation.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
Rayon (cellulose acetate) is a semisynthetic polymer obtained by chemically modifying natural cellulose. It has superior lustre, smoothness, and durability compared to raw cotton, making the Assertion true.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason and Link
Acetylation of cellulose (with acetic anhydride in the presence of sulphuric acid) converts it into cellulose acetate (rayon), which significantly improves its mechanical strength and aesthetic appearance. Thus, the Reason is true and directly explains the Assertion.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both Assertion and Reason are correct statements, and Reason explains the Assertion.

questiontext.text:
47. Assertion : Most of the Synthetic polymers are not biodegradable.

Reason : Polymerisation process induces toxic character in organic molecules.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
Most synthetic polymers (such as polythene, PVC, and polystyrene) possess strong, inert carbon-carbon backbones that cannot be broken down by microbial enzymes, so they are non-biodegradable. Hence, the Assertion is true.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason
Polymerisation does not induce toxic character in organic molecules; in fact, many polymers are chemically inert and non-toxic. Their non-biodegradability is due to resistance to enzymatic cleavage rather than toxicity. Hence, the Reason is false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Assertion is a correct statement and Reason is a wrong statement.

questiontext.text:
48. Assertion : Olefinic monomers undergo addition polymerisation.

Reason : Polymerisation of vinylchloride is initiated by peroxides/ persulphates.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
Olefinic monomers (alkenes and their substituted derivatives) contain carbon-carbon double bonds (\(\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}\)) that open up to undergo chain-growth addition polymerisation. Hence, the Assertion is true.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason and Link
The free-radical addition polymerisation of vinyl chloride (\(\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{CHCl}\)) is indeed initiated by radical initiators such as peroxides or persulphates. However, this specific initiation example does not explain the general reason why olefinic monomers undergo addition polymerisation (which is due to the presence of \(\pi\)-bonds). Hence, both statements are true, but Reason does not explain Assertion.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Assertion and Reason both are correct statements, but Reason does not explain Assertion.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_AR_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q49 - High tensile strength of polyamides as fibres

questiontext.text:
49. Assertion : Polyamides are best used as fibres because of high tensile strength.

Reason : Strong intermolecular forces (like hydrogen bonding within polyamides) lead to close packing of chains and increase the crystalline character, hence, provide high tensile strength to polymers.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
Polyamides (such as Nylon 6,6 and Nylon 6) possess high tensile strength and are widely used as thread-forming fibres. Hence, the Assertion is true.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason and Link
Polyamides contain polar \(-\mathrm{CONH}-\) groups that form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds between adjacent polymer chains. This leads to close packing of chains, higher crystallinity, and consequently high tensile strength. Thus, the Reason is true and correctly explains the Assertion.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both Assertion and Reason are correct statements, and Reason explains the Assertion.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_AR_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q50 - Synthesis of synthetic rubber vs natural rubber

questiontext.text:
50. Assertion : For making rubber synthetically, isoprene molecules are polymerised.

Reason : Neoprene (a polymer of chloroprene) is a synthetic rubber.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
Natural rubber is a polymer of isoprene (2-methyl-1,3-butadiene). Synthetic rubbers are homopolymers of 1,3-butadiene derivatives (such as chloroprene) or copolymers of 1,3-butadiene with styrene or acrylonitrile—not polymerised isoprene. Hence, the Assertion is false.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason
Neoprene is formed by the free-radical polymerisation of chloroprene (2-chloro-1,3-butadiene) and is a well-known synthetic rubber. Hence, the Reason is true.

questiontext.text:
51. Assertion : Network polymers are thermosetting.

Reason : Network polymers have high molecular mass.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
Network (cross-linked) polymers possess extensive covalent cross-links between chains, forming a rigid three-dimensional structure that becomes infusible on heating; thus, they are thermosetting. Hence, the Assertion is true.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason and Link
Network polymers indeed have high molecular mass, as do all macromolecules. However, having a high molecular mass is not the reason they are thermosetting (linear thermoplastics also have high molecular mass); rather, it is their extensive covalent cross-linking. Thus, both statements are correct, but Reason does not explain Assertion.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Assertion and Reason both are correct statements, but Reason does not explain Assertion.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_AR_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q52 - Use of polytetrafluoroethene in non-stick cookwares

questiontext.text:
52. Assertion : Polytetrafluoroethene is used in making non-stick cookwares.

Reason : Fluorine has highest electronegativity.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
Polytetrafluoroethene (Teflon) is chemically inert, thermally stable, and has a very low coefficient of friction, so it is widely used to coat non-stick cookwares. Hence, the Assertion is true.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason and Link
Fluorine has the highest electronegativity among all elements. While both statements are true, the high electronegativity of fluorine alone does not directly explain the non-stick property of Teflon (which arises from its strong \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{F}\) bonds, symmetric non-polar chain surface, and very weak intermolecular forces with other substances). Hence, Reason does not explain Assertion.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Assertion and Reason both are correct statements, but Reason does not explain Assertion.
